q: Through the Antarctic winter, which emperor penguin parent keeps the egg warm on its feet?
explain: The female hands the egg over and heads to sea to feed, while the male balances it on his feet under a warm fold of skin for about two months.

source.title: Emperor penguin breeding cycle

searchNote: AAD breeding-cycle page: emperors build no nest; the male balances the egg on his feet under his brood pouch for 60 to 64 days while the female feeds at sea. WHOI page says males incubate on their feet for two months.

q: While fasting through incubation, male emperor penguins can lose about how much of their body weight?
explain: Males can't feed while holding the egg, so the long winter fast takes a heavy toll: they often lose as much as half their body weight.

source.title: Penguins - Smithsonian Ocean Portal

searchNote: Smithsonian Ocean penguins page says incubating males often lose as much as half their body weight. AAD Mawson station notes say fathers have fasted for about 4 months by the time chicks appear.

q: Besides the emperor penguin, which penguin also incubates its single egg on its feet instead of in a nest?
explain: Like emperors, king penguins build no nest; the single egg is kept warm balanced on top of a parent's feet.

source.title: Penguins - Smithsonian Ocean Portal

searchNote: Search summary of the Smithsonian penguins page noted the egg-on-feet incubation is shared by emperor and king penguins; a king penguin study in the results also said king penguins build no nest and incubate a single egg on their feet. Gentoos build stone nests and little penguins use burrows.

q: How do male emperor penguins get through the Antarctic winter while incubating eggs?
choices: Sheltering in burrows dug in snow
Taking turns feeding at sea every few days
explain: Incubating males crowd together in huddles and stay that way all winter, through every temperature and wind.

source.title: Halley Diary — August 2004 - British Antarctic Survey

searchNote: British Antarctic Survey Halley diary describes the male emperors spending all winter huddled through all temperatures and winds; AAD pages say males cannot feed while carrying the egg.

q: In 2022, which Antarctic penguin received protection under the US Endangered Species Act?

q: About how wide can a wandering albatross's wings stretch, tip to tip?

q: What happens to an Atlantic puffin's colorful bill after the breeding season?
choices: It sheds its bright outer plates
It grows a hard knob on top
It turns from gray to bright orange
explain: Both sexes grow bright plates on the bill each spring for courtship, then shed them, leaving a smaller, duller bill for winter at sea.

q: What happens when ultraviolet light shines on a breeding Atlantic puffin's beak?
explain: Streaks on the breeding bill fluoresce a bright cyan-green under UV light, which may act as a signal to potential mates.

source.title: Puffins Amp Up Their Sex Appeal With Glowing Beaks

searchNote: Audubon news article reports that if you shine ultraviolet light on a puffin in breeding plumage, streaks on its beak glow a bright cyan-green; the plates are UV-reactive.

q: How does an Atlantic puffin keep hold of a beakful of fish while it catches more?
choices: It stores the fish in a stretchy throat pouch
It skewers the fish on its hooked bill tip
Its tongue pins fish against spines in its mouth
